title: Quantum reference frames beyond subsystems: a reconstruction and generalization of the perspective-neutral framework
authors: Stefan L. Ludescher, Manuel Mekonnen, Thomas D. Galley, Markus P. Mueller
abstract: We generalize the notion of quantum reference frames (QRFs) to cases where the frame does not necessarily correspond to a tensor factor subsystem, but to a covariant quantum instrument. This unlocks a variety of physical applications: "frames of labeling" for indistinguishable particles, suggesting explanations for the symmetrization postulate and the absence of parastatistics, and yielding a transparent description of the entanglement of bosons and fermions; and relational clocks reproducing the Schrödinger equation exactly even when all subsystems are interacting or when there are frequency superselection sectors. Our work generalizes the perspective-neutral approach to QRFs pioneered by Höhn and co-authors, which we reconstruct from a simple operational scenario. We give a resource-theoretic grounding of this framework, and show how the notion of completely covariant operations explains the relevance of the charge-zero sector and the pure-state transformation behavior across perspectives. This also suggests operational clarifications of some aspects of constraint quantization, e.g. of the meaning of constraint equations such as $C|ψ\rangle=0$. Some of our results, such as our generalization of relationalization maps to instruments, apply more broadly to other QRF frameworks too, and they contribute to bridging the gap between operational quantum information theory and the internal QRF research program.
summary: This paper revolutionizes the concept of Quantum Reference Frames by generalizing them from simple subsystems to covariant quantum instruments. By imposing strict operational constraints based on complete covariance, it derives fundamental physical principles, offering novel explanations for particle statistics and time evolution in complex, interacting quantum systems.
main_problem: The work generalizes Quantum Reference Frames (QRFs) beyond simple tensor factor subsystems to covariant quantum instruments, aiming for a unified operational understanding of perspectival quantum mechanics.
main_result: This generalized framework provides explanations for the symmetrization postulate, entanglement description between bosons and fermions, and allows relational clocks to reproduce the Schrödinger equation even in interacting systems.
method: The authors reconstruct and generalize the perspective-neutral approach by imposing the operational constraint that only completely covariant operations can be physically implemented on a system.
model_or_system: The framework analyzes quantum systems using QRFs, extending from subsystem descriptions to general covariant quantum instruments. Applications include modeling indistinguishable particles and relational time evolution in interacting many-body settings.
key_observables: Completely covariant operations, constraint equations (e.g., C|ψ> = 0), and the resulting effective Hamiltonians for relative motion.
important_parameters: The structure of the symmetry group G (generalized from finite to compact Lie groups) and interaction coupling constants K.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that physical reality must be describable solely through completely covariant operations, which dictates the allowed measurements and dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper first reconstructs the perspective-neutral framework operationally before generalizing it to covariant instruments. It then details applications concerning indistinguishable particles, entanglement, and relational time evolution in interacting systems.
why_interesting: It provides a deep operational foundation for defining physical observables (like time or particle labels) when standard subsystem decompositions fail due to interactions or global symmetries, which is crucial for advanced many-body theory.

The only change is that B is replaced by the composite system BC, where C is an ideal reference frame. The mere role of C is to define what it means that some structure of B “points in some direction”, i.e. to break the symmetry while catalytically preserving its own local pure state.
